prerequisites: Operational knowledge of: functions, limits, derivatives, integrals, differentials.
Operational knowledge of: partial derivatives, differentials of functions of several variables, differential equations.
Knowledge of the mathematics program of the scientific high school.
Operational knowledge of: study of functions, tables and graphs, equations and inequalities, algebraic systems, trigonometry, limits, derivatives and integrals.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the laws of electromagnetism underlying industrial engineering.
Mental attitude suitable for tackling a physical problem.
Ability to simplify the problem with appropriate schematizations.
Ability to identify the important physical laws for understanding a phenomenon.
Understanding the connections between the different laws of mechanics and electromagnetism.
Ability to translate the relevant physical laws into mathematical formulas.

Ability to apply knowledge of physical laws to identify, formulate and solve monodisciplinary problems in related subjects, but already with a view to interdisciplinary problems in industrial engineering.
Development of an adequate technical expression and discussion of one's own arguments.
Respect commitments and deadlines.
Understanding of the theoretical and experimental bases of classical and modern physics.
Familiarity with the scientific method of inquiry and its application.
Solve problems by applying the main laws of physics and mathematical knowledge to describe real physical systems.
Analyze data using appropriate statistical tools.
Work individually and in groups and actively participate in the formulation of working hypotheses and their planning and implementation.
Design different approaches to problem-solving and autonomously evaluate the best procedure.
Draft reports concerning the results of a physics study.
Record procedures and operations performed to allow others to repeat or check the results produced.
Use technical language correctly.
Lifelong learning.

syllabus_topics: Electric charge, Coulomb's law, Superposition Principle, electric field, Gauss's theorem, electric potential, electrostatic energy, properties of conductors, Coulomb's theorem, electric capacitance, capacitors, properties of dielectrics, definition of current, continuity equation, electromotive force, steady currents: DC electrical circuits, Kirchhoff's principles, Ohm's law, non-steady currents: RC circuits, magnetic field, Lorentz force, Biot-Savart law, Laplace's formulas, forces on current-carrying conductors, Ampère's law, energy of magnetic and electric fields, Faraday's law, self and mutual induction, RL circuits, displacement current, complete Maxwell's equations.
Introduction to Physics: Scientific method, physical quantities and units of measurement, scalars and vectors.

Kinematics of the material point: Description of motion in three dimensions (position, velocity, acceleration) and examples (rectilinear motion, circular motion, parabolic motion, cycloid). Change of reference system.

Dynamics of the material point: Newton's laws and applications. Forces and examples (inclined plane, simple pendulum, harmonic motion). Sliding and viscous friction. Apparent forces. Momentum. Energy, work and conservation principles. Equilibrium and stability.

Extended bodies: Systems of material points and rigid bodies. Center of mass. Kinematics and roto-translational motions. Angular momentum. Moment of inertia. Cardinal equations. Statics and dynamics of rigid bodies. Compound pendulum. Pure rolling.

Mechanics: Vectors; Kinematics: description of motion in three dimensions and at three levels (position, velocity, acceleration) with various examples, kinematics of rigid bodies, change of reference system; Statics: forces and their moments, equilibrium of the material point and rigid body, cardinal equations of statics, center of mass, examples of ideal constraints, friction between solid bodies; Dynamics: principle of inertia, second principle of dynamics, mass and density, momentum and impulse, Kepler's laws and Newton's universal law of gravitation, solution of various problems of material point dynamics, non-inertial reference frames and apparent forces, principle of action and reaction, conservation of momentum and angular momentum, collisions, cardinal equations of dynamics, center of mass, moment of inertia, solution of various problems of system dynamics. Work, principle of virtual work, theorem of live forces, kinetic energy, symbolic equation of statics, conservative forces, stationarity of potential energy and stability of equilibrium, conservation of mechanical energy with various application examples.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test to ascertain the skills acquired by the student in solving electromagnetism and mechanics problems, and an oral test to ascertain the student's knowledge of the course program. Grades range from 18 to 30 with honors. An insufficient grade is given for severe conceptual errors or lack of understanding. A grade of 29-30 and cum laude is given for complete, in-depth knowledge and flexible, autonomous operation.
